mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate exceeding 9.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically reduces consumer spending and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 9.0%, the S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline of HOUST and RSAFS does not produce negative S&P 500 20-day returns with a Rank IC above 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of simultaneous labor market deterioration (UNRATE > 9.0%) and industrial contraction (INDPRO < 95.0), the S&P 500 tends to underperform over the next 60 trading days due to broad economic weakness.
failure_condition: When UNRATE > 9.0% and INDPRO < 95.0, the S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts rate below 500 thousand units signals weak residential construction and reduced consumer confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST is below 500.0, the S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in employment (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a severe labor market contraction, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in PAYEMS and rise in UNRATE does not correlate with negative S&P 500 20-day returns (Rank IC < 0.03) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising retail sales figure (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer spending, which supports corporate earnings growth and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When RSAFS is rising, the S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 0.5% signals the onset of monetary tightening, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS rises above 0.5%, the S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.
